newsitem.title: USA: Merck says forex trims Q4, yr sales growth by 1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Merck says forex trims Q4, yr sales growth by 1 pct.

text.p: Merck & Co Inc said Tuesday foreign exchange cut its fourth quarter and 12-month sales growth by one percent, leaving sales of human and animal health products 18 percent higher for the period.

Fourth quarter profits remained strong despite the drag, up 24 percent to $0.87 a share compared to $0.60 last year. The growth was fueled by strong unit volume gains, Merck chairman Raymond Gilmartin said in a statement.
Total sales rose 19 percent for the year. Merck said the divestitures in 1995 of Kelco and Medco Behavioral Care Corp reduced sales slightly.
Sales outside the United States fell slightly on a percentage basis to 30 percent of 1996 sales compared to 1995's 32 percent, Merck said.
"Sales growth for the quarter and the year was led by established major products, 1995 and 1996 product introductions and growth from the Merck-Medco Managed Care business," Gilmartin said.
Merck said its cholesterol-lowering drugs Zocor and Mevacor hold over 40 percent of the worldwide market -- sold to over 7.5 million patients in more than 90 countries.
It said sales of Zocor, which aims to prevent heart attacks in people with high cholesterol and heart disease, grew strongly, making it the leading HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor.
In a nod toward hopes of further growth, the company said less than 30 percent of patients with coronary disease currently receive cholesterol-lowering therapy.
Mevacor is the first cholesterol-lowering drug shown to regress atherosclerotic plaques in the carotid arteries of patients without known coronary artery disease, the company said.

Merck said Vasotec, its angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor for reducing high blood pressure and preventing disability and death due to heart failure, continued to grow and is the leading branded ACE inhibitor product worldwide.

The company said U.S. prescription sales remain strong for Pepcid, an H2-receptor antagonist for the treatment of duodenal ulcers and the short-term treatment of gastric ulcers and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).
In the fourth quarter, the drug became the second most-prescribed prescription H2-receptor antagonist in the United States, Merck said.

In the U.S. over-the-counter market, Pepcid AC Acid Controller, sold by a joint venture between Johnson & Johnson and Merck, continues to lead the acid-control market, despite heavy competition, the company said.
